assets.title: AI Acceptable Use Policy
assets.summary: Baseline policy for approved AI tool use in a fictional SMB.

instruction.body: Before using an AI tool, classify the requested work by data sensitivity, approved surface, and action risk. Refuse to place restricted or confidential material in unapproved model contexts. Prefer retrieval with citations over unstated memory. Escalate if the user requests credential exposure, hidden policy bypass, or unapproved external posting.
constraints: Do not expose secrets or credentials.
Do not post externally on behalf of a user without explicit approval.
Do not use restricted content in broad exports.
failureModes: Treating a convenience request as consent to share private data.
Answering from memory when cited retrieval is required.
instruction.escalation: Ask an admin to review requests involving confidential data or external publication.

humanDocument.body:
# AI Acceptable Use Policy

Use AI tools only on approved work, approved data, and approved surfaces. Keep secrets out of model context. Prefer cited retrieval when answering policy or operational questions. External posting and high-risk actions require explicit approval.

assets.title: Personal Data Removal Guide
assets.summary: Guide for removing direct personal identifiers before AI use.

instruction.body: Remove or mask direct personal identifiers before including support records in an AI prompt. Replace names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, account IDs, and ticket IDs with stable placeholders. Preserve the operational meaning needed to complete the task.
constraints: Do not drop facts required to solve the support task.
Do not invent replacement details.
Keep placeholder labels consistent within the same request.
failureModes: Masking only obvious names while leaving ticket IDs or email addresses.
Changing the operational meaning of a customer issue.
instruction.escalation: Escalate if redaction would remove the evidence needed for a regulated complaint.

humanDocument.body:
# Personal Data Removal Guide

Mask direct identifiers before AI use. Preserve the facts needed for the job. Use consistent placeholders and record what was removed.

assets.title: Incident Triage Playbook
assets.summary: Agent-first operational playbook for initial incident triage.

instruction.body: Classify the incident by customer impact, blast radius, reversibility, and evidence freshness. Build a concise timeline from observed facts only. Recommend the next diagnostic command or system read-back before proposing a fix.
constraints: Do not claim root cause before evidence supports it.
Do not recommend destructive remediation without an explicit rollback path.
failureModes: Skipping current-state verification.
Confusing a symptom with root cause.
instruction.escalation: Escalate when customer-facing production impact is confirmed.

humanDocument.body:
# Incident Triage Playbook

Start with impact, blast radius, reversibility, and evidence freshness. Build a timeline from facts. Verify current state before fixing.

assets.title: Pull Request Review Agent Skill
assets.summary: Agent instruction for prioritizing code review findings.

instruction.body: Review pull requests by leading with bugs, regressions, security issues, and missing tests. Ground each finding in a concrete file and line. Keep summaries secondary. Say clearly when no material issue is found.
constraints: Do not nitpick style without behavioral risk.
Do not claim tests were run unless evidence is provided.
failureModes: Overweighting summaries over actionable findings.
Missing a permission or data-leakage regression.

humanDocument.body:
# Pull Request Review Agent Skill

Prioritize real defects and risks. Cite files and lines. Keep summary short. Be explicit about unverified areas.

assets.title: Agent Task Brief Template
assets.summary: Reusable structure for assigning work to an agentic system.

instruction.body: When preparing an agent task brief, include goal, context, constraints, source of truth, non-goals, acceptance checks, stop conditions, and expected deliverables. Keep the brief short enough to be used directly in an agent harness.
constraints: Do not include secrets.
Do not include ambiguous success criteria without naming the ambiguity.

humanDocument.body:
# Agent Task Brief Template

- Goal
- Context
- Constraints
- Source of truth
- Non-goals
- Acceptance checks
- Stop conditions
- Deliverables

assets.title: Reader Navigation Guide
assets.summary: Plain-language guide for finding approved material in the reader interface.

instruction.body: When helping a reader find material, route them to the published reader library first. Use the page tree to narrow by asset type, then use header search when the reader knows a term but not the page location. Do not send reader users to management controls unless they are also responsible for editing or approving content.
constraints: Keep reader instructions separate from operator workflows.
Do not expose draft, restricted, or internal-only records to reader users.
failureModes: Treating the reader as a content manager.
Assuming search is better than the page tree for broad browsing.
instruction.escalation: Ask a content manager when a reader cannot find expected published material.

humanDocument.body:
# Reader Navigation Guide

Use the left page tree when you want to browse the published library by category. Open a folder, choose a page, and read the approved version in the main pane.

## When to use search

Use the header search when you remember a phrase, policy name, or topic. Search is best for targeted lookup. Browsing is better when you need to understand what material exists.

## What readers should see

Readers should see active, approved pages that are safe for the published web surface. Drafts, review queues, permissions, exports, API diagnostics, and operator settings belong in the control interface.

## If something is missing

If a page appears missing, ask a content manager to verify status, lifecycle state, allowed surfaces, and permissions.

assets.title: Asset Lifecycle States Reference
assets.summary: Reference page explaining draft, active, deprecated, archived, and restricted states.

instruction.body: Interpret lifecycle state as the primary publishing signal. Draft material is not ready for broad reader use. Active approved material may be shown on allowed surfaces. Deprecated material should be used only when no replacement exists. Archived material is retained for history. Restricted material requires explicit permission checks before retrieval, export, or display.
constraints: Do not treat approved status alone as sufficient for reader publication.
Always combine lifecycle, status, sensitivity, and allowed surface.
failureModes: Publishing a draft because it has a human-readable body.
Exporting restricted content because it appears in search results.

humanDocument.body:
# Asset Lifecycle States Reference

Lifecycle state tells readers and agents how a governed asset should be treated.

## Draft

The page is being written or reviewed. Drafts are not reader-ready.

## Active

The page is current and may be used when status, sensitivity, permission, and allowed surface also permit use.

## Deprecated

The page is still available for historical context, but teams should prefer a replacement.

## Archived

The page is retained for audit or history and should not guide new work.

## Restricted

The page requires additional permission checks before display, export, or execution.

assets.title: Support Summary Checklist
assets.summary: Checklist for turning a support thread into a safe summary.

instruction.body: Convert support threads into short summaries by separating customer claim, observed evidence, product area, account impact, prior troubleshooting, and requested next step. Remove personal data before AI use and cite the source ticket or transcript identifier only when the view allows it.
constraints: Do not include raw contact details.
Do not turn customer speculation into a confirmed fact.
Do not omit prior troubleshooting that changes the next action.
failureModes: Summarizing sentiment but dropping reproduction steps.
Leaving personal identifiers in copied transcript text.
instruction.escalation: Escalate when the support issue involves legal, billing, or regulated data.

humanDocument.body:
# Support Summary Checklist

Use this checklist when a support conversation needs to become safe, structured context for an AI helper.

## Required sections

1. Customer claim
2. Observed evidence
3. Product area
4. Account or workflow impact
5. Prior troubleshooting
6. Open questions
7. Recommended next step

## Personal data requirement

Remove names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ticket IDs, and account IDs unless the target view explicitly allows them. Preserve the operational facts needed to solve the issue.

## Quality check

A good support summary lets another person or AI helper understand what happened, what has been tried, and what should happen next without reading the full thread.

assets.title: Customer Escalation Brief Playbook
assets.summary: Playbook for producing a concise, factual escalation brief from governed source material.

instruction.body: Build an escalation brief from verified facts only. Start with current customer impact, then timeline, evidence, owner, next decision, and risk. Distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions. Include citations or source references for claims that drive the escalation.
constraints: Do not assign blame.
Do not hide uncertainty.
Do not promise a fix date unless approved by the accountable owner.
failureModes: Writing a status update instead of a decision brief.
Merging assumptions into the evidence timeline.
instruction.escalation: Escalate to the incident owner when customer impact is ongoing or scope is unclear.

humanDocument.body:
# Customer Escalation Brief Playbook

Use this playbook when a customer issue needs a clear, factual escalation path.

## Brief structure

- Current impact
- Timeline of verified events
- Evidence and citations
- Accountable owner
- Next decision needed
- Risks and unknowns

## Writing standard

Use short, direct sentences. Separate facts from assumptions. Name uncertainty instead of filling gaps.

## Exit criteria

The brief is ready when a decision maker can see what happened, who owns the next step, and what risk remains.

assets.title: AI Use Boundaries Policy
assets.summary: Policy for deciding what company information AI tools may use.

instruction.body: Before using company information with AI, verify sensitivity, approved location, user permission, purpose, and whether export is requested. Demo material may be used broadly. Internal material requires a signed-in business purpose. Restricted, confidential, and secret material require explicit permission and the smallest useful excerpt.
constraints: Use the smallest context that can answer the request.
Do not include credentials, tokens, or raw secrets.
Do not export material unless export is explicitly allowed.
failureModes: Treating an authenticated session as blanket permission.
Copying full source documents when a cited excerpt is enough.
instruction.escalation: Escalate any request involving regulated data, credentials, or third-party publication.

humanDocument.body:
# AI Use Boundaries Policy

Before using company information with an AI tool, verify the material, the person, the purpose, and where the information will go.

## Required checks

- Sensitivity
- Approved location
- User permission
- Purpose
- Export intent

## Practical rule

Use the smallest useful excerpt. A short cited passage is usually better than a full document. Never include credentials or raw secrets.

## High-risk cases

Escalate requests that involve regulated data, hidden policy bypass, external publication, or broad exports.

assets.title: Grounded Answer Template
assets.summary: Reusable answer format for AI responses that need citations and uncertainty handling.

instruction.body: Answer with a short conclusion, supporting evidence, cited sources, and uncertainty. If the source set is insufficient, say what is missing instead of guessing. Keep recommendations separate from verified facts.
constraints: Do not invent citations.
Do not hide missing evidence.
Do not present recommendations as source-backed facts.
examples: Answer: The approved policy allows public-demo material on web surfaces. Evidence: asset sensitivity and allowed surface both permit web display.
failureModes: Confidently answering from incomplete retrieval.
Mixing facts, assumptions, and recommendations in one paragraph.

humanDocument.body:
# Grounded Answer Template

Use this structure when an answer needs to be traceable.

## Answer

State the conclusion in one or two sentences.

## Evidence

List the source-backed facts that matter.

## Citations

Name the governed assets or excerpts that support the answer.

## Uncertainty

Say what is unknown, stale, missing, or inferred.

## Recommendation

If a recommendation is needed, keep it separate from the verified facts.

assets.title: Citation Quality Standard
assets.summary: Quality bar for citations in reader-facing and agent-facing answers.

instruction.body: Use citations that point to the smallest source unit needed to verify a claim. Prefer current active approved assets. Mark stale, deprecated, or restricted sources clearly. Do not cite a source that only loosely resembles the claim.
constraints: Citations must support the exact claim.
Avoid citation padding.
Call out source limitations when evidence is indirect.
failureModes: Citing a broad policy when a specific SOP is required.
Using old material without noting deprecation or review risk.

humanDocument.body:
# Citation Quality Standard

A citation should let a reader verify the claim quickly.

## Good citations

- Point to the smallest useful source unit
- Support the exact claim
- Prefer current, active, approved assets
- Include limitations when evidence is indirect

## Poor citations

- Link to a broad document without pointing to the relevant idea
- Cite a source that is only topically related
- Hide that a source is stale, deprecated, or permission-limited

## Review question

Could a reader use this citation to confirm the sentence without reading unrelated material?

assets.title: Release Readiness Overview
assets.summary: Human-readable overview of the synthetic release readiness process.

instruction.body: Use the release readiness overview as human-readable context only. When deciding whether a release can proceed, require evidence for tests, permissions, rollback, telemetry, and owner approval. Do not treat this overview as a substitute for the release checklist.
constraints: Do not approve a release based on narrative alone.
Do not skip rollback or telemetry evidence.
failureModes: Confusing an overview with the checklist.
Ignoring missing evidence because the release looks small.
instruction.escalation: Escalate when release evidence is missing or rollback is unclear.

humanDocument.body:
# Release Readiness Overview

Release readiness means the team can explain what changed, prove the change works, observe it after deploy, and roll it back if needed.

## Required evidence

- Scope of change
- Test results
- Permission and data boundary review
- Deployment target
- Rollback path
- Owner approval
- Post-deploy observation plan

## Reader expectation

A reader should be able to understand the release at a glance without seeing internal control screens.

## Not a checklist

This overview explains the concept. The release owner still needs to complete the operational checklist before promoting a release.

assets.title: Search Query Planning Tool Instruction
assets.summary: Instruction for forming narrow search queries against governed assets.

instruction.body: Before calling search, convert the user need into two or three focused queries. Use asset names, known policy terms, and required action words. Avoid broad single-word searches. After results return, compare source type, lifecycle state, and citation fit before answering.
constraints: Do not over-retrieve when one precise query is enough.
Do not answer from search snippets without opening the source when detail matters.
failureModes: Using vague terms that return unrelated policy pages.
Choosing the first result even when lifecycle or sensitivity is wrong.

humanDocument.body:
# Search Query Planning Tool Instruction

Good search starts before the tool call.

## Plan the query

Turn the request into focused terms. Include asset names, policy words, workflow names, or action words when they are known.

## Run narrow searches first

A precise query is easier to verify than a broad one. Use two or three variants when the vocabulary is uncertain.

## Evaluate results

Check title, type, lifecycle state, sensitivity, and citation fit. Do not answer from a result that only seems related.

assets.title: Internal AI Release Checklist

instruction.body: Before promoting an agent instruction bundle, confirm the source stable IDs, review status, lifecycle state, retrieval eligibility, and rollback owner. Internal release notes may reference fictional deployment windows and dry-run package hashes, but they must not be included in public demo exports.
constraints: Do not promote draft or reviewing assets.
Do not include internal-only release notes in demo packages.
Record the package name used for any internal export.
failureModes: Treating internal visibility as demo eligibility.
Skipping rollback ownership before release.
instruction.escalation: Escalate to a maintainer if an internal release needs demo distribution.

humanDocument.body:

assets.title: Reader Access and Export Rules
assets.summary: Approved page that readers can open, while exports remain a separate choice.

metadata.exportReason: Readable in the demo but intentionally omitted from demo-agent-pack.

instruction.body: Use this demo page to explain read access separately from export access. A general reader query for emergency password access may use this asset only to verify that restricted page IDs are omitted; it must not include restricted procedures or export-blocked content in demo-agent-pack.
constraints: Do not add this asset to demo-agent-pack.
Do not include restricted stable IDs in public export output.
Explain no-export state without revealing restricted procedure details.
failureModes: Assuming readable demo pages can always be exported.
Using a readable asset to smuggle restricted proof content into an export.

humanDocument.body:
# Reader Access and Export Rules

This page explains the difference between reading a page in ForgetBase and exporting that page into a package for AI tools.

## Short version

Readers can open this page in the knowledge base. Export packages are handled separately. A page can be safe to read in the browser and still be left out of an export.

## When this matters

Use this rule when a team wants broad read access but tighter control over copied material. For example, a policy owner may want everyone to read the latest guidance while limiting which pages can be bundled into an AI package.

## What readers see

Readers see the approved page title, summary, owner, update date, review state, and readable body. They can search and ask questions from pages they are allowed to use. They should not see export controls, review queues, API keys, or admin settings.

## What exports include

Exports include only pages that are approved for the requested package. Export access is checked separately from read access. If a page is excluded, the export should explain that the page was skipped without revealing restricted details.

## Owner checklist

- Confirm the page is approved before readers can use it.
- Decide whether the page can be included in each export package.
- Keep restricted procedures out of public demo exports.
- Review access and export settings before release notes or demos.

## If something looks wrong

Ask a content manager to check the page status, allowed surfaces, export packages, and permission grants. Do not assume that browser access means export access.

assets.title: Restricted Security Escalation Runbook

instruction.body: credential vault escalation requests must be handled as restricted synthetic incidents. Confirm the caller has a restricted security grant before returning operational details. If the caller has only general reader or demo access, state that the runbook is restricted and provide no procedural steps.
constraints: Do not export this runbook to demo-agent-pack or demo packages.
Do not reveal restricted steps to unauthorized API, CLI, MCP, web, or export consumers.
Use synthetic owner names only.
failureModes: Returning restricted procedural steps in a public search answer.
Including this runbook in OKF or JSON public packages.

This synthetic restricted runbook validates that emergency access details are blocked from general reader retrieval and public export packages.
